extracted.intended_audience: taxonomists / naturalists / museum zoologists identifying and describing freshwater bryozoa (Indian region)
extracted.subtask_description: Morphological identification and taxonomic delimitation of freshwater phylactolaemate bryozoans (genera and species, esp. Plumatellina) including specimen preparation and illustration guidance. Focused on diagnostic characters of divisions, families, genera and species and on methods for examining statoblasts and zoaria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division diagnostic characters: Plumatellina vs Cristatellina
rubrics_metrics.description: Division I, PLUMATELLINA, nov.--Ectocyst well developed; zoaria without a special organ of progression; polypides contained in tubes. Division II, CRISTATELLINA, nov.--Ectocyst absent except at the base of the zoarium which is modified to form a creeping 'sole'; polypides embedded in a common synoecium of reticulate structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use presence/absence and distribution of ectocyst, the presence of a creeping sole, and whether polypides are in individual tubes or embedded in a common synoecium to separate the two divisions. Note that the Cristatellina here is represented by a single genus (Cristatella).

rubrics_metrics.name: Family character set: Fredericellidae
rubrics_metrics.description: Zoaria dendritic; zooecia distinctly tubular, with the ectocyst well developed; statoblasts of one kind only, each surrounded by a chitinous ring devoid of air-spaces; polypides with the lophophore circular or oval when expanded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These structural features diagnose the family Fredericellidae (single genus Fredericella). Use statoblast morphology (single kind, no air-spaces) together with lophophore shape and ectocyst condition to recognize the family.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family character set: Plumatellidae
rubrics_metrics.description: Phylactolæmata which have horseshoe-shaped lophophores and a well-developed ectocyst not specialized to form an organ of progression. Some or all of the statoblasts are provided with a 'swim-ring' consisting of symmetrically disposed, polygonal chitinous chambers containing air.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize Plumatellidae by the horseshoe-shaped lophophore and the presence (in some or all statoblasts) of a swim-ring of air-containing chambers. Combine internal anatomy (lophophore) and statoblast construction for family-level ID.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subfamily distinctions: Plumatellinæ vs Lophopinæ
rubrics_metrics.description: Subfamily A. PLUMATELLINÆ: Zoarium dendritic or linear, firmly fixed to extraneous objects; zooecia tubular, not fused together to form a gelatinous mass. Subfamily B. LOPHOPINÆ: Zoarium forming a gelatinous mass in which the tubular nature of the zooecia almost disappears, capable to a limited extent of progression along a smooth surface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use whether zooecia are distinct tubular units fixed to substrates (Plumatellinæ) versus embedded/fused in a gelatinous synoecium with limited progression (Lophopinæ) to separate subfamilies; statoblast armature and colony habit are also diagnostic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key characters for genus-level identification in Plumatellidæ
rubrics_metrics.description: Couplet-style key characters: I. Statoblasts without marginal processes — A. Zooecia cylindrical, not embedded in gelatinous investment (Plumatellinæ): a. Zooecia arising directly from one another; no stolon; free statoblast oval = PLUMATELLA. a'. Zooecia arising singly or in groups from an adherent stolon; free statoblasts oval = STOLELLA. B. Zooecia cylindrical, embedded in a structureless gelatinous investment; zooecia arising from a ramifying stolon; statoblasts circular = [STEPHANELLA]. C. Polypides embedded in a hyaline synoecium that conceals the cylindrical form of the zooecia (Lophopinæ): c. Polypides upright... = LOPHOPUS; c'. Polypides recumbent... = [AUSTRALELLA]. II. Statoblasts armed with hooked processes (Lophopinæ): A. Processes confined to extremities; zoaria separate = LOPHOPODELLA. B. Processes entirely surrounding statoblast; many zoaria embedded in common gelatinous investment = PECTINATELLA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply statoblast armature (presence/absence of marginal processes), whether zooecia are embedded in gelatinous investment, stolon presence, and polypide orientation to determine genus. The key is hierarchical; follow couplets stepwise and examine statoblasts and colony structure carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genus Plumatella diagnostic characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Zoarium dendritic, recumbent, erect, or partly recumbent and partly erect. Zooecia tubular, not confined in a gelatinous synoecium; the ectocyst usually horny. Statoblasts often of two kinds, free and stationary, the latter without air-cells and as a rule adherent by one surface, the former provided with a well-developed ring of air-cells but without marginal processes, oval in form, never more than about 0.6 mm. in length. Polypide with less than 65 tentacles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize Plumatella by combination of colony habit, tubular zooecia with horny ectocyst, and the two statoblast types (free with swim-ring vs fixed without air-cells). Beware of compacted/vertical forms (historically called Alcyonella) which may represent phases rather than distinct genera.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species-level characters in the Indian Plumatella key
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary characters used in the key: ectocyst condition (more or less stiff vs stiff vs swollen and contractile), tip shape of zooecia when polypide retracted (rounded vs truncated), presence/absence and prominence of emargination and furrow, surface ornament (minutely roughened/annulate), and proportions/outline of free statoblast swim-ring (narrower on sides vs ends). These characters are organized into couplets leading to species names (e.g., fruticosa, emarginata, javanica, diffusa, allmani, tanganyikæ, punctata).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a combination of ectocyst texture/colour, zooecial shape (including emargination/furrow and L-shaped zooecia), and statoblast morphology to separate species. The key stresses patterns and typical characters rather than isolated oddities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precaution 1: Dissect tangled zoaria
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) If the zoarium appears to be tangled, if the branches intertwine or overlap, or if the zooecia are closely pressed together, the whole mass should be carefully dissected out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dissect specimens that appear tangled because different species' zoaria can be entangled and the characteristic branching and zooecial shape may be obscured. Failure to do so can lead to misidentification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precaution 2: Examine as large a part as possible
rubrics_metrics.description: (2) As large a part as possible of each zoarium should be examined, preferably with a binocular microscope, and allowance should be made for irregularities and abnormalities of all kinds. What must be observed is the rule rather than the exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base identifications on the predominant/typical characters across a sizeable portion of the colony rather than on small or abnormal fragments. Use binocular microscopy to observe branching patterns and overall colony habit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precaution 3: Statoblast orientation during examination
rubrics_metrics.description: (3) When the statoblasts are being examined, care must be taken that they lie flat and that their surface is parallel to that of the nose-piece of the microscope. If they are viewed obliquely it is impossible to see their true outlines and proportions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure statoblasts are properly oriented (flat and parallel to objective) to correctly assess outline and swim-ring proportions; oblique views distort morphology and lead to mismeasurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precaution 4: Rendering statoblasts transparent to assess swim-ring proportions
rubrics_metrics.description: (4) In order to see the relative proportions of the capsule and the swim-ring it is necessary that the statoblast should be rendered transparent. This is often difficult owing to the presence of air in the air-cells, but strong nitric acid applied judiciously will render it possible (p. 240).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use chemical clearing (strong nitric acid, applied judiciously) to make statoblasts transparent and reveal true relationships of capsule and swim-ring; take care with handling and artifact introduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustration principle: faithful representation
rubrics_metrics.description: I have impressed upon the artist the importance of representing what he saw rather than what he thought he ought to see, and the figures are very close copies of actual specimens. I have deliberately chosen for representation specimens of Plumatella preserved by the simple methods which are often the only ones that it is possible for a traveller to adopt...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrations should be faithful, accurate copies of observed specimens (including specimens preserved by simple methods). Prioritize accurate depiction over idealized forms so that typical field-preserved specimens can be recognized by readers.
